situation: A charity running a children's literacy program funded by a grant.
complication: The interim report is due next month and must show progress and spending against the grant.
key_question: What should the interim report tell the funder about progress and spending?

titles.situation: The grant is part spent and the interim report is due.
titles.options: Two ways to present progress to the funder.
titles.recommendation: Report progress plainly and flag budget moves early.
titles.roadmap: Draft, review, then send the report before it is due.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the grant ends on target.
titles.risks: The main risk is reporting a budget move the funder did not expect.

work.title: Interim report: progress and spending
work.for: The funder's program officer, report section for the executive director to review
body: Progress. The program has reached [F4] children so far against our commitment of [F3] for the year, which is [F7] of the goal. {How tutoring is delivered and any highlights, for the program lead to add.}
Spending. We have spent [F2] of the [F1] grant, which is [F5]. The remaining [F8] will fund {planned uses of the remaining funds, for the program lead to confirm against the budget tracker}.

Budget lines. {Any planned moves between budget lines, for the executive director to confirm, or a line saying none are planned.} Any move will stay within the [F9] the funder allows without approval, and we will ask you before any larger change.
We would be glad to talk through any part of this report.
